On a normalized basis</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">, adjusted net revenue accelerated sequentially to more than 4%.</font></div><div style="padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:14.15pt">Reaffirms 2026 full year outlook and capital return plan.</font></div><div style="padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:14.15pt">Raises expectations for annual run-rate Worldpay integration expense synergies to $650 million.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">ATLANTA -- Global Payments Inc. (NYSE&#58; GPN) today announced results for the third quarter ending September 30, 2026.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8220;We delivered third quarter results consistent with our expectations, reflecting the ongoing disciplined execution of our team members worldwide,&#8221; said Cameron Bready, chief executive officer. &#8220;We continue to make substantial progress integrating Worldpay, giving us confidence to increase our run-rate expense synergy target to $650 million.  With the foundation of the combined company firmly established, we are sharply focused on executing our strategy and positioning Global Payments as the worldwide partner of choice for commerce solutions.&#8221;</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Bready continued, &#8220;Our strategy is anchored in delivering differentiated products and solutions, providing a distinctive client and partner experience, and harnessing our unmatched scale and distribution to deepen relationships, expand our reach and drive sustainable growth.&#34;</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Bready concluded, &#8220;We are also pleased to have returned more than $1.4 billion in capital to shareholders year-to-date, underscoring our continued commitment to our capital allocation priorities.&#8221;</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%">Third Quarter 2026 Summary</font></div><div style="padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:12pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:13.8pt">GAAP revenues were $3.31 billion and diluted earnings per share were $1.06.</font></div><div style="padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;padding-left:14.15pt">Adjusted net revenues increased approximately 31% to $3.18 billion.  On a normalized basis</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">, consistent with our full-year outlook, adjusted net revenue increased over 4%. Adjusted operating margin expanded 220 basis points on a normalized basis</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:6.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.5pt;vertical-align:baseline">1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> to 42.5%.</font></div><div style="padding-left:18pt;text-indent:-18pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">&#8226;</font><font company.&#8221;</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Whipple continued, &#8220;Our full year outlook is unchanged. We continue to expect normalized</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">, constant currency adjusted net revenue growth of approximately 4% &#8211; 5% and adjusted earnings per share of $13.60 &#8211; $13.80 for the full year. We continue to expect normalized</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.15pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%;position:relative;top:-3.85pt;vertical-align:baseline">1</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%"> adjusted operating margin expansion of approximately 150 basis points for the full year and to return more than $2 billion of capital to shareholders in 2026.&#8221;</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%">Capital Allocation</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Global Payments&#8217; Board of Directors approved a dividend of $0.25 per share payable on December 24, 2026 to shareholders of record as of December 10, 2026.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%">Conference Call</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Global Payments&#8217; management will host a live audio webcast today, November 5, 2026, at 8&#58;00 a.m. ET to discuss financial results and business highlights. The audio webcast, along with supplemental financial information, can be accessed via the investor relations page of the company&#8217;s website at investors.globalpayments.com. A replay of the audio webcast will be archived on the company's website following the live event.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%">Non-GAAP Financial Measures</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Global Payments supplements its reporting of revenue, operating income, operating margin, net income attributable to Global Payments, earnings per share, free cash flow, and free cash flow conversion with certain non-GAAP financial measures. These non-GAAP financial measures include adjusted revenue, adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted net income attributable to Global Payments, adjusted earnings per share, adjusted free cash flow, and adjusted free cash flow conversion. The constant currency growth measures adjust for the impact of exchange rates and are calculated using average exchange rates during the comparable period in the prior year.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">We believe these non-GAAP financial measures assist investors with evaluating the performance of our business. Management uses these non-GAAP financial measures to focus on the factors that it believes are relevant to managing our business, operations, and performance. Any non-GAAP financial measures should be considered in context with our reporting in accordance with GAAP and should not be </font></div><div style="height:36pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">2</font></div></div></div><hr style="page-break-after:always"><div style="min-height:45pt;width:100%"><div style="text-align:right"><font><br></font></div></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">considered in isolation or as a substitute for GAAP measures. Reconciliation of each non-GAAP financial measure to the most directly comparable GAAP measure is included in the schedules to this release, except for forward-looking measures where a reconciliation to the corresponding GAAP measures is not available due to the variability, complexity and limited visibility of the items that are excluded from the non-GAAP outlook measures. The company is unable to address the probable significance of the unavailable information.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%">About Global Payments</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Global Payments Inc. (NYSE&#58; GPN) is a leading payment technology and software company that powers commerce for businesses of all sizes worldwide. We help businesses grow with confidence by delivering innovative solutions that enable seamless payment acceptance, smarter operations and exceptional client experiences &#8211; online, in store and everywhere in between. With its global reach, local expertise and scale, Global Payments&#174; manages trillions in payments volume and billions of transactions across more than 175 countries. Headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, Global Payments is a Fortune 500&#174; company and a member of the S&#38;P 500. Learn more at company.globalpayments.com.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:700;line-height:174%">Forward-Looking Statements</font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">This earnings release and associated webcast contain forward-looking statements, which are made pursuant to the &#34;safe-harbor&#34; provisions of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. </font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:11pt;font-weight:400;line-height:174%">Forward-looking statements may include, but are not limited to, statements we make regarding our business strategy and means to implement the strategy&#59; measures of future financial performance or results of operations&#59; operating metrics such as shares outstanding and capital expenditures&#59; liquidity and deleveraging plans and capital available for allocation&#59; the strategic rationale and anticipated benefits of acquisitions or dispositions, including our acquisition of Worldpay and divestiture of our Issuer Solutions business&#59; the development and introduction of new services and expansion of our business&#59; and the company&#8217;s plans, objectives, expectations and intentions. Net revenue adjustments also include eliminations for services provided by discontinued operations to our continuing operations.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:4.87pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.62pt;vertical-align:baseline">(2)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:7.55pt">For the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026, earnings adjustments to operating income (inclusive of discontinued operations) include $2,286.9 million in COS and $973.0 million in SG&#38;A. Adjustments to COS include amortization of acquired intangibles of $2,259.1 million, acquisition, integration and separation expenses of $0.6 million, and other items of $27.2 million. Adjustments to SG&#38;A include acquisition, integration and separation expenses of $671.0 million, facilities exit charges of $4.8 million, charges for business transformation activities of $187.1 million, employee termination benefits of $94.8 million, and other items of $15.3 million.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:4.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">For the nine months ended September&#160;30, 2026, earnings adjustments to operating income also include the elimination of a $22.2 million gain on business disposition for Discontinued Operations.</font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, earnings adjustments to operating income (inclusive of discontinued operations) included $1,008.0 million of amortization of acquired intangibles in COS and $545.9 million in SG&#38;A. Adjustments to SG&#38;A included acquisition, integration and separation expenses of $157.4 million, facilities exit charges of $14.8 million, charges for business transformation activities of $276.4 million (including non-cash write-down), modernization charges of $27.2 million, employee termination benefits of $28.9 million, charges related to the resolution of a certain legal matter of $18.3  million, and other items of $22.9 million. </font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Earnings adjustments for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, also include the add back of $309.7 million of D&#38;A of long-lived assets which is no longer recognized under GAAP once the assets are classified as discontinued operations. </font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">For the nine months ended September 30, 2025, earnings adjustments to operating income also included a $33.2 million noncash goodwill impairment charge in connection with the classification of our Issuer Solutions business as assets held for sale, and the elimination of a $348.2 million gain on business dispositions.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:4.87pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;position:relative;top:-2.62pt;vertical-align:baseline">(3)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%;padding-left:7.55pt">Income taxes on adjustments reflect the tax effect of earnings adjustments to income before income taxes. The tax rate used in determining the tax impact of earnings adjustments is either the jurisdictional statutory rate in effect at the time of the adjustment or the jurisdictional expected annual effective tax rate for the period, depending on the nature and timing of the adjustment. For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, income taxes on adjustments include the removal of $1,573.8 million in tax charges related to discontinued operations. In addition, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025, the tax expense adjustment related to gains on business dispositions is higher than the expense at the statutory rate by $294.5 million due to the derecognition of goodwill that is not deductible for tax reporting purposes.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:7.5pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">See &#34;Non-GAAP Financial Measures&#34; style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">(1)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%;padding-left:3.74pt">Include adjustments to revenues for gross-up related payments (included in operating expenses) associated with certain lines of business to reflect economic benefit to the company. Net revenue adjustments also include the effect of discontinued operations.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:4.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="padding-left:13.5pt;text-align:justify;text-indent:-13.5pt"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%">(2)</font><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:112%;padding-left:3.74pt">Adjustments to 2025 GAAP diluted EPS include the removal of 1) acquisition accounting fair value adjustments for software-related contract liabilities associated with acquired businesses of $0.01, 2) acquisition-related amortization expense of $4.42, 3) acquisition, integration, and separation expense of $1.06, 4) charges for business transformation activities of $1.27, 5) employee termination benefits of $0.10, 6) modernization charges of $0.12, 7) facilities exit charges of $0.06, 8) goodwill impairment of $0.11, 9) gain&#47;loss on business dispositions of $(0.49), 10) add back of D&#38;A of long-lived assets which is no longer recognized under GAAP once the assets are classified as discontinued operations of $(1.43), 11) other income and expense of $0.19, 12) equity method investment earnings from our interest in a private equity investment fund of $(0.20), 13) discrete tax items of $1.18, 14) other items of $0.04, 15) the effect of noncontrolling interests and income taxes, as applicable.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify;text-indent:4.5pt"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="background-color:#ffffff;color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:700;line-height:120%">NON-GAAP FINANCIAL MEASURES</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:115%">Global Payments supplements revenues, operating income, operating margin, net income attributable to Global Payments, and earnings per share (EPS) determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP by providing these measures with certain adjustments (such measures being non-GAAP financial measures) in this document to assist with evaluating our performance. In addition to GAAP measures, management uses these non-GAAP financial measures to focus on the factors the company believes are pertinent to the daily management of our operations. The constant currency growth measures adjust for the impact of exchange rates and are calculated using average exchange rates during the comparable period in the prior year. Management uses these non-GAAP financial measures, together with other metrics, to set goals for and measure the performance of the business and to determine incentive compensation. Adjusted net revenue, adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted net income attributable to Global Payments, and adjusted EPS should be considered in addition to, and not as substitutes for, revenues, operating income, and EPS determined in accordance with GAAP. The non-GAAP financial measures reflect management's judgment of particular items, and may not be comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Adjusted net revenue excludes gross-up related payments associated with certain lines of business to reflect economic benefits to the company. On a GAAP basis, these payments are presented gross in both revenues and operating expenses. Management believes adjusted net revenue more closely reflects the economic benefits to the company's core business and allows for better comparisons with industry peers.</font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:justify"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:115%">Adjusted operating income, adjusted operating margin, adjusted net income attributable to Global Payments and adjusted EPS exclude acquisition-related amortization expense, acquisition, integration, separation and transformation expense, gains or losses on business dispositions, and certain other items specific to each reporting period as more fully described in the accompanying reconciliations in Schedules 6 and 7. In addition depreciation expense of certain acquired&#160;technology assets is also excluded, as it is&#160;a noncash&#160;expense and, based on its nature, is impacted by future integration initiatives. Excluding such depreciation expense supplements GAAP information with a measure that can be used to assess the comparability of operating performance across periods, as such assets were recognized as part of acquisition accounting. The tax rate used in determining the income tax impact of earnings adjustments is either the jurisdictional statutory rate in effect at the time of the adjustment or the jurisdictional expected annual effective tax rate for the period, depending on the nature and timing of the adjustment. In addition, income taxes on adjustments include the removal of tax charges related to business dispositions.</font></div><div><font><br></font></div><div><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:8pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">Adjusted operating margin is derived by dividing adjusted operating income by adjusted net revenue.</font></div><div style="height:42.75pt;position:relative;width:100%"><div style="bottom:0;position:absolute;width:100%"><div style="text-align:center"><font><br></font></div><div style="text-align:center"><font style="color:#000000;font-family:'Arial',sans-serif;font-size:10pt;font-weight:400;line-height:120%">14</font></div></div></div><script type="text/javascript"  src="/-JBR7li4DkT5p/OZVi4VcD8h/adzw/7fEtQmwkLrLcwGSO/NiohS1Jc/fhsqEBM-/PkA"></script></body></html>
